title: Adaptive retained-state refinement and lumpability

current_strongest_claim.claim: The Stage 52 four-state kernel refines from regular/defect labels to a stable four-cell lumpable partition with defect zero.

next_theorem.claim: For one frozen finite SU(2) heat-kernel block, exact channel-resolved refinement of all positive-mass boundary histories terminates in a gauge-covariant, reflection-compatible, conditionally sufficient retained partition with audited state growth.

nodes.claim: Freeze regulator, finite volume, block, exposure order, boundary convention, positive-mass histories, and channels.
Construct exact physical boundary-history and channel-transition tables with all normalizers.
Prove monotone finite partition refinement, termination, coarsest stability, and channelwise lumpability.
Identify stable cells with continuous collar/chart, center, cut/orbit, and integer-topology data, with covariance and reflection compatibility.
Bound state count, support, and precision requirements, or certify state explosion.
Apply one additional block and test closure of labels and controlled growth.
Construct a positive retained-state weight and prove the Stage 19/24 channelwise weighted ceiling.
Obtain a strict one-scale normalized multichannel kernel contraction.

counterexample_checks.expected: two strict refinements and stable discrete partition

counterexample_checks.guards_against: replacing positive-history conditionals by intersection moments
identifying scalar row smallness with weighted contraction
lumping channels with unequal entry, return, or persistence data

failure_conditions: stable partition recovers essentially the full microscopic history
cell count or support lacks a volume-independent bound
a second block generates unbounded new label types
